text:
Maya: Heads-up — PM asked for a single Console view that shows per-model/region/deployment counts for timeouts, 5xx, OOM, and degraded-mode/fallbacks. We need to decide metric ownership and a shape for the telemetry before they build the dashboard mockups.
Sam: For visibility: propose these metric names (emitted by runtime when possible):
- runtime.request.errors_total{error_type=\"timeout|5xx|oom|fallback\", model=..., region=..., deployment_id=...} (counter)
- runtime.request.fallback_count_total{fallback_reason=..., model=..., region=..., deployment_id=...} (counter)
- runtime.request.latency_p50_p95_p99{model=..., region=...} (histogram/summary)
Priya: runtime can emit errors_total for timeout/5xx/oom. Fallbacks are often decided at the proxy/router layer (we add circuit-breaker fallbacks, model-variant fallbacks), so fallback_count_total should be emitted by the router/proxy with fallback_reason and route_policy labels. Keep label set minimal to avoid high cardinality.
Oliver: Concern about cardinality — deployment_id + model + region + fallback_reason could explode. We should mandate aggregation tiers in the ingestion layer: ingest -> aggregate_to_daily{model,region,error_type} and also keep a limited set of high-cardinality timeseries for short retention (7d) for debugging.
Jess: On Console side, we want to show per-route and per-model panels with filters. We need consistent label names so queries are reusable. Also UX needs an indicator for \"degraded mode\" vs \"hard-error\" (degraded = we served fallback or partial content). Can we add a label degraded=\"true|false\" or is that duplicative with error_type=fallback?
Priya: degraded=true is useful; runtime can set degraded=true for cases where a graceful fallback was returned (e.g., cached response or limited tokens). But fallback_reason captures semantics (e.g., quota_breach, oom, model_unavailable). We should avoid both error_type=fallback and degraded=true being ambiguous — define: error_type in {timeout,5xx,oom,internal} and degraded=true/false or fallback_reason present when degraded=true.
Sam: Proposal for data contract:
- runtime.request.errors_total (counter) labels: model, region, deployment_id (optional), error_type
- runtime.request.degraded_total (counter) labels: model, region, deployment_id (optional), degraded=true, fallback_reason (optional)
- router.fallbacks_total (counter) labels: route, policy, fallback_reason, model, region
- ingestion: two derived views — detailed short-retention (7d) and rolled-up long-retention (90d) aggregated by model+region+error_type
Rae: We should also emit an event stream for individual fallback incidents for the incident timeline (not just counters). That helps SRE correlate to traces and logs.
Oliver: We need to decide which team owns the dashboard panels and alerts. My suggestion: eng-runtime emits metrics; eng-infra/ingest owns aggregation/derived views; eng-platform owns Console panels and alert definitions; eng-sre owns SLO alerts. Agree?
Jess: Yes. For rollout UX: Console should show a feature-flagged beta \"reliability insights\" workspace. We'll surface the short-retention detailed view as a \"Drilldown\" link and default the top-level dashboard to aggregated metrics to avoid cost/slow queries.
Sam: Implementation notes:
- Add metric definitions to telemetry repo with examples and prometheus-style unit conventions.
- Ingest team to add a transform job that dedupes events (same request_id) and emits aggregated counters. Deduping rule: prefer runtime-origin errors; router-origin fallbacks are separate metric sets.
- Add canary: emit the new labels under feature flag for 1% of traffic for 48h, validate cardinality and query cost.
Priya: I'll open runtime PR to start emitting errors_total and degraded_total with the agreed label set. Will add feature flag gate and tests. CC: @ingest-bot to create an ingestion schema ticket.
ingest-bot: Created ticket INGEST-412: \"Derived views for errors/degraded/fallbacks — schema + aggregation\". Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INGEST-412
Maya: Action items:
- Priya: runtime PR for errors/degraded (due EOD Thu)
- Ingest: INGEST-412 owner to post ETA and aggregation plan by Mon
- Jess: Console mockups for aggregated + drilldown by Mon for product review
- Oliver/SRE: recommend alert thresholds for 5xx and degraded rate (TBD)
- Sam: add telemetry docs and sampling/canary plan (EOD Fri)
Rae: Quick clarification — how do we count OOMs? Is it only process OOMs (OOM killer) or also model OOM responses (e.g., model returns error code)? We should separate: oom_type=process|model. Otherwise debugging is hard.
Priya: Good call — runtime will add oom_type label when known. If unknown, oom_type=unknown.
Oliver: One more: add a boolean label 'user_visible_error' true/false to distinguish errors surfaced to caller vs internal retry/fallbacks. That helps product dashboards.
Maya: This is great — please add comments to INGEST-412 and link the runtime PR when ready. We'll coordinate a short async review session tomorrow 10am PST to finalize metric names and the canary rollout plan. :thumbsup:
Sam: ack.
Priya: ack, will start PR.
Jess: I'll start the mockups and add initial panel wireframes to the ticket.
ingest-bot: INGEST-412 updated with initial aggregation sketch.
Maya: Thanks everyone — will follow up with calendar invite for the async review slot.
